lines.text: One tiny byte of overflow in Ruby could let attackers take over websites.
The letter ß has no capital in many old encodings. Ruby writes two letters, SS, instead.
lines.title: The odd letter

lines.text: Ruby checks room for only one byte. Enough of these letters spill past the end of the memory.
lines.title: How it goes wrong

lines.text: An input with 21 of these letters is enough to overflow by one byte.
lines.title: The trigger

lines.text: Rails and classic Sinatra apps are affected by default. GitLab and GitHub Enterprise had no fix yet.
lines.title: Who is exposed

lines.text: Upgrade Ruby soon. A public attack demo is planned for November 25.
